entries.title: Proverbs 25:1
segments: ¶These [are] also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:2
segments: ¶[It is] the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings [is] to search out a matter.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:3
segments: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings [is] unsearchable. {is...: Heb. there is no searching}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:4
segments: ¶Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:5
segments: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:6
segments: ¶Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great [men]: {Put...: Heb. Set not out thy glory}

words.text: [men]: {Put...: Heb. Set not out thy glory}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:7
segments: For better [it is] that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.

words.text: hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower

entries.title: Proverbs 25:8
segments: ¶Go not forth hastily to strive, lest [thou know not] what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

words.text: , lest [thou know not] what to do

entries.title: Proverbs 25:9
segments: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour [himself]; and discover not a secret to another: {a secret...: or, the secret of}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:10
segments: Lest he that heareth [it] put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:11
segments: ¶A word fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in pictures of silver. {fitly...: Heb. spoken upon his wheels}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:12
segments: [As] an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [so is] a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:13
segments: ¶As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, [so is] a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:14
segments: ¶Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift [is like] clouds and wind without rain. {of a...: Heb. in a gift of falsehood}

words.text: . {of a...: Heb. in a gift of falsehood}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:15
segments: ¶By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:16
segments: ¶Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

words.text: for thee, lest thou be filled

entries.title: Proverbs 25:17
segments: ¶Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and [so] hate thee. {Withdraw...: or, Let thy foot be seldom in} {weary...: Heb. full of thee}

words.text: thee. {Withdraw...: or, Let thy foot be seldom in} {weary...: Heb. full of thee}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:18
segments: ¶A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour [is] a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:19
segments: ¶Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble [is like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:20
segments: ¶[As] he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, [and as] vinegar upon nitre, so [is] he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:21
segments: ¶If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

entries.title: Proverbs 25:22
segments: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:23
segments: ¶The north wind driveth away rain: so [doth] an angry countenance a backbiting tongue. {driveth...: or, bringeth forth rain: so doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance}

words.text: . {driveth...: or, bringeth forth rain: so doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance}

entries.title: Proverbs 25:24
segments: ¶[It is] better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:25
segments: ¶[As] cold waters to a thirsty soul, so [is] good news from a far country.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:26
segments: ¶A righteous man falling down before the wicked [is as] a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:27
segments: ¶[It is] not good to eat much honey: so [for men] to search their own glory [is not] glory.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:28
segments: ¶He that [hath] no rule over his own spirit [is like] a city [that is] broken down, [and] without walls.
